item.title: Carbon-neutral algal bloom management via algal organic matter repurposing
item.dc:creator: Jianguo Zhang
Wenlin Jia
Yunxiao Jian
Lulu Qu
Shuang Zhao
item.description:
Authors: Jianguo Zhang, Wenlin Jia, Yunxiao Jian, Lulu Qu, Shuang Zhao
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Algal organic matter (AOM) has been considered a typical pollutant in algal bloom waters, conventionally managed through flocculation-flotation processes with high carbon footprints. This study presents a paradigm shift by redefining AOM as a functional crosslinker and developing an AOM-induced self-driven flotation (A-SDF) strategy. The approach utilizes active groups in AOM (-COOH/-OH) coordinated with trace amounts of metal coagulants to construct multilevel gel flocs with Al 2 O 3 /FeO(OH) crystalline phases. Remarkably, these flocs not only capture algal cells but also activate dissolved oxygen (DO), inducing DO enrichment-interfacial gas nucleation behavior (DOE-IGNB) and leading to microbubbles (MBs) formation at the floc interface under mild turbulence. The process achieved efficient removal of algal cells (82–95%), turbidity (86–95%), and AOM (45–79%) within 2 min without external aeration. Compared with existing technologies, the carbon footprint, treatment time, and economic cost were reduced by 66.08–96.90%, 71.67–96.00%, and 50.55–97.67%, respectively, while residual metal concentrations remained well below drinking water standards. Density functional theory calculations confirmed strong DO adsorption by tetrahedral AlO 4 /FeO 4 lattices as the molecular mechanism driving DOE-IGNB. By repurposing AOM as a resource and activating endogenous DO, this work provides a universal carbon-neutral pathway for sustainable algal bloom management worldwide.

item.title: Exploring enhanced self-esteem reactivity in response to social prediction errors in adolescence
item.dc:creator: Klara Gregorova
Geert-Jan Will
Pia Burkard
Marcel Romanos
Andrea M. F. Reiter
item.description:
Authors: Klara Gregorova, Geert-Jan Will, Pia Burkard, Marcel Romanos, Andrea M. F. Reiter
Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 11997
Abstract: Abstract Self-esteem is a cornerstone of mental health across the lifespan. Throughout life, but particularly during adolescence, self-esteem is shaped by social appraisals. Previous work in adults has shown that momentary fluctuations in self-esteem are explained not only by whether we are liked by others but also by whether we are liked more or less than expected (social prediction errors). Here, we examine age-related differences in how social experiences shape self-esteem in 141 participants aged 10-40 years using an experimental social evaluation task and ecological momentary assessment. In the experiment, self-esteem reactivity to unexpected social feedback follows a non-linear age-related pattern, peaking in late adolescence. In daily life, self-esteem reactivity to perceived pleasantness of social interaction and naturalistic social prediction errors is stronger in younger participants. Individual differences in experimental and daily-life self-esteem reactivity are associated, highlighting heightened self-esteem malleability during adolescence.

item.title: Excited-state twisted intramolecular charge transfer enables reversible light control of rhodamine-graphene binding
item.dc:creator: Giovanni M. Beneventi
Yilin He
Xuliang Qian
Matteo Andrea Lucherelli
Martina Hartinger
Konstantin Benthues
Norbert Jux
Alejandro Cadranel
item.description:
Authors: Giovanni M. Beneventi, Yilin He, Xuliang Qian, Matteo Andrea Lucherelli, Martina Hartinger, Konstantin Benthues, Norbert Jux, Alejandro Cadranel, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Reversible light control of supramolecular interactions underpins fundamental processes in nature, inspiring artificial molecular devices and adaptive materials. Existing approaches rely on light-modulated interconversion between ground-state species characterized by distinct binding properties. Here, we introduce twisted intramolecular charge transfer (TICT) as an excited-state specific lever to modulate dye–surface adhesion. Using rhodamine B base (Rhb) as the photoactive species, we combine femtosecond spectroscopy with theoretical calculations to provide a direct observation of TICT formation and its thermal equilibrium with the locally excited state. We show that the associated dihedral twisting and charge redistribution weaken Rhb-graphene binding, enabling light-induced dye desorption in water. Molecular dynamics simulations corroborate that the out-of-plane TICT conformations induce steric hindrance against the graphene basal plane, significantly reducing the binding affinity and lowering the thermodynamic barrier of the dye-surface desorption. This synergy between experiment and theory establishes excited-state conformational dynamics as a general strategy to control supramolecular interactions in host-guest systems in physiological conditions, with implications for sensing, delivery, and materials science.

item.title: Preventing data leakage in neural decoding
item.dc:creator: Robert Wong
Michael H. McCullough
Tianfeng Lu
Shuyu I. Zhu
Geoffrey J. Goodhill
item.description:
Authors: Robert Wong, Michael H. McCullough, Tianfeng Lu, Shuyu I. Zhu, Geoffrey J. Goodhill
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Neural decoding is a widely-used machine learning technique for investigating how behavior, perception and cognition are represented in neural activity. However without careful application data leakage can occur, where information from the test set contaminates the training set, leading to biased estimates of decoding performance and potentially invalidating biological conclusions. Here we show that leakage can be introduced in neural decoding studies by common supervised and unsupervised preprocessing steps, including dimensionality reduction. We reveal that in some cases leakage can paradoxically decrease decoding performance relative to unbiased estimates, and we provide theoretical analyses explaining how this occurs. We also show that, for autocorrelated neural time series, randomized k-fold cross-validation can dramatically overstate decoding performance. Based on these findings, we provide detailed recommendations for avoiding data leakage in neural decoding.

item.title: Achieving high-yield and pilot-scale synthesis of nano graphene oxide via photochemical defect engineering and oxidative cleavage
item.dc:creator: Yuchen Yang
Chen Ma

Weiming Huang

item.description:
Authors: Yuchen Yang, Chen Ma, Jiangbin Hong, Weiming Huang, Ming Lin, Jianting Zhang, Wenhua Chen, Nanzhi Zheng, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 11913
Abstract: Abstract The high-yield synthesis of nanoscale graphene oxide is increasingly critical, yet widespread scalable implementation of top-down methods remains hindered by low efficiency. Here, we report a highly efficient, scaled-up approach coupling photochemical defect engineering and oxidative cleavage to fragment micron-sized graphene oxide into nanoscale flakes. Irradiation induces nanoscale holes on the graphene oxide basal plane, causing rapid fragmentation upon hydrogen peroxide treatment. This yields nanoscale graphene oxide (20 to 60 nanometers) featuring an sp 2 -hybridized carbon core and carboxylic acid-rich edges. The material exhibits exceptional stability against thermal ripening, prolonged solar irradiation, and chemical reduction. Achieving an 85 ± 5 % conversion yield, the practical scalability of this process is demonstrated using a pilot-scale device with a projected annual capacity of 0.52 tons of powder. This work provides a route for the pilot-scale production of high-performance nanoscale graphene oxide materials.

item.title: A wearable reconfigurable surface electrode network for spatiotemporal control of hand motor output
item.dc:creator: Kening Gong
Li Jiang
Siyang Qiu
Xueai Li
Ming Cheng
Xiaoran Tang
Changhao Yan
Lijia Guo
item.description:
Authors: Kening Gong, Li Jiang, Siyang Qiu, Xueai Li, Ming Cheng, Xiaoran Tang, Changhao Yan, Lijia Guo, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Transcutaneous electrical stimulation can elicit hand movements by activating peripheral nerves and muscles. Here, we present a wearable system integrating programmable constant-current stimulation, a flexible 32-electrode forearm array with full-array active–return routing, and real-time path and parameter updating. Human-derived skin–electrode load tests showed a mean current-delivery accuracy of 94.0%, while four-hour reassessment showed 93.5% within-participant action-category agreement. Using reconfigurable active–return routing and an anatomy-informed two-level traversal strategy, we established current-path-to-action maps spanning 12 wrist and hand action categories, with spatial patterns broadly consistent with superficial forearm flexor and extensor compartments. Data-glove and inertial measurements quantified parameter-dependent finger-joint responses and action-specific wrist rotations. The mapped actions were sequentially combined for feedback-guided, stimulation-assisted task-level hand operation, supporting wearable functional electrical stimulation for task-oriented hand assistance and rehabilitation research.

item.title: Basal mantle motion causes Pacific hotspot drift
item.dc:creator: Xianzhi Cao
Sanzhong Li
Nicolas Flament
Yanhui Suo
Zhaoxia Jiang
Heda Wang
Dingshan Deng
Qiuling Liu
item.description:
Authors: Xianzhi Cao, Sanzhong Li, Nicolas Flament, Yanhui Suo, Zhaoxia Jiang, Heda Wang, Dingshan Deng, Qiuling Liu
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Hotspot-based reference frames are foundational to plate reconstructions yet increasing evidence indicates that individual Pacific hotspots have migrated over time. How the overall motion of Pacific hotspots relates to the evolution of the underlying Pacific basal mantle structure (BMS), the inferred source of Pacific mantle plumes, remains elusive. Here we combine plate reference frame analysis with global mantle flow simulations to quantify the average motion of Pacific hotspots and compare it with the predicted motion of the Pacific BMS. Comparisons between Pacific fixed-hotspot reference frames and other absolute reference frames suggest an average southward migration of Pacific hotspots of ~5–10° from 80 Ma. Mantle flow models driven by plate reconstructions independently predict comparable southward average migration of Pacific plumes and the underlying Pacific BMS. In the models, the coupled BMS-plume migration is driven by greater subduction flux along the northern Pacific than along the southern Pacific between ~80-45 Ma, which generated persistent southward lower-mantle flow. Our results indicate that the average drift of Pacific hotspots is linked to the motion of the Pacific BMS, highlighting dynamic coupling between surface hotspot motion and basal mantle evolution.

item.title: Diabetes subtyping without HbA1c enhances identification of severe insulin-deficient diabetes
item.dc:creator: Martin Schön
Oana P. Zaharia
Christian Binsch
Huishu Lin
Claudia H. T. Tam
Cadmon K. P. Lim
Gechang Yu
Klaus Strassburger
item.description:
Authors: Martin Schön, Oana P. Zaharia, Christian Binsch, Huishu Lin, Claudia H. T. Tam, Cadmon K. P. Lim, Gechang Yu, Klaus Strassburger, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 12003
Abstract: Abstract Data-driven subtyping of diabetes can be affected by disease duration and treatment. We propose a modified procedure waiving the use of HbA1c, and only using BMI, age at diagnosis, insulin secretion and insulin sensitivity. Participants of the German Diabetes Study (GDS, N = 940), the Ludwigshafen Risk and Cardiovascular Health (LURIC) cohort ( N = 794) and the Hong Kong Diabetes Biobank (HKDB) ( N = 7959) were subtyped by including (w/HbA1c) and then by leaving out HbA1c (w/oHbA1c). In GDS, subtyping w/oHbA1c increased the prevalence of severe insulin-deficient diabetes (SIDD) from 3.3% to 22.1%. Cumulative incidence of diabetic retinopathy differed when comparing SIDD and the other clusters using both approaches (w/HbA1c: SIDD 16.1%, P log-rank = 0.027; w/oHbA1c: SIDD 14.4%, p log-rank < 0.001), with higher discriminative ability w/oHbA1c (AUROC: 0.74 vs 0.66 w/HbA1c, p = 0.049). The discrimination of future insulin secretion failure in SIDD was also better w/oHbA1c ( p AUROC = 0.011). In LURIC, subtyping w/oHbA1c also increased the prevalence of SIDD from 3.0% to 11.3% and showed lower all-cause mortality for SIDD compared to insulin resistant ( p = 0.035) and age-related ( p = 0.005) diabetes subtypes. Finally, in HKDB, subtyping w/oHbA1c also increased the prevalence of SIDD from 29.2% to 35.7% without attenuating its association with diabetic retinopathy, supporting preserved subtype discrimination in an independent cohort. The refined algorithm excluding HbA1c improves the detection of the diabetes subtype with severe insulin deficiency and its complications in already treated persons, although further validation in more diverse populations is needed to establish its broader generalizability.

item.title: Mechanistic insights into intracellular phase separation and maturation of FUS LC revealed by in-cell NMR
item.dc:creator: Maiki Tamura
Qingci Zhao
Yusuke Yamaguchi
Manami Yasuda
Fumiyoshi Ishidate
Takahiro Fujiwara
Noritaka Nishida
item.description:
Authors: Maiki Tamura, Qingci Zhao, Yusuke Yamaguchi, Manami Yasuda, Fumiyoshi Ishidate, Takahiro Fujiwara, Noritaka Nishida
Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 11791
Abstract: Abstract Fused in sarcoma (FUS) forms dynamic biomolecular condensates through phase separation, a process associated with stress responses and neurodegenerative diseases. Here, we use in-cell NMR spectroscopy to directly observe condensate formation of the FUS low-complexity (LC) domain in living cells. We identify a two-step process: initial droplet formation followed by time-dependent maturation, characterized by reduced internal mobility. Deletion mutant analysis reveals that while initial condensate formation is driven by collective multivalent interactions, the reversible amyloid core (RAC) region is essential for the subsequent maturation. Intracellular droplets form at concentrations well below the in vitro threshold, which cannot be explained by macromolecular crowding alone. Notably, droplet formation is suppressed under nutrient starvation, suggesting that ATP-dependent cellular activities indirectly promote FUS condensation. These findings demonstrate that the metabolically active intracellular environment modulates FUS condensate behavior, providing mechanistic insights into early events in pathological aggregation and establishing a general framework for studying condensates in cells.

item.title: A small RNA regulates iron homeostasis and host mucus colonization in Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron
item.dc:creator: Thomas Guest
Ryan T. Fansler
Gianluca Prezza
Gohar Mädler
Hannah Schlauch
Wenhan Zhu
Alexander J. Westermann
item.description:
Authors: Thomas Guest, Ryan T. Fansler, Gianluca Prezza, Gohar Mädler, Hannah Schlauch, Wenhan Zhu, Alexander J. Westermann
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Symbiotic bacteria in the human intestinal microbiota provide many pivotal functions to human health and occupy distinct biogeographic niches within the gut. Yet the molecular basis underlying niche-specific colonization remains poorly defined. To address this, we conducted a time-resolved dual RNA-seq experiment to simultaneously monitor the transcriptional co-adaptations of human commensal Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron and human gut epithelial cells in a hypoxic, mucus-producing, epithelial co-culture system. Comparative transcriptomic analysis of mucus-associated versus supernatant Bacteroides populations unveiled small RNAs (sRNAs) that are differentially regulated between spatially segregated subpopulations. Among these, we identified IroR as a key sRNA that facilitates B . thetaiotaomicron adaptation to iron limitation and host glycan availability, partly by modulating expression of capsule-associated surface states. This work provides new insights into the spatiotemporal dynamics of gut colonization and underscores a previously underappreciated role for bacterial sRNAs in shaping mutualistic interactions between the human microbiota and the gut epithelium.

item.title: CD300LD drives osteoclastogenesis and inflammatory bone loss by sensing cholesterol and activating FES SYK STAT3
item.dc:creator: Bolei Li
Yiling Li
Siyue Lai
Yue Li
Kaixin Yan
Xudong Wang
Kai Bao
Jinyi Ma
item.description:
Authors: Bolei Li, Yiling Li, Siyue Lai, Yue Li, Kaixin Yan, Xudong Wang, Kai Bao, Jinyi Ma, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Osteoclasts are essential for bone remodeling and homeostasis. Their excessive activation drives pathological bone loss disorders such as periodontitis and arthritis. Current osteoclast-inhibiting therapies are limited by adverse effects and poor specificity, underscoring the importance to identify new regulators of osteoclastogenesis. Here, we conducted a pooled CRISPR–Cas9 screen targeting cluster of differentiation (CD) genes to uncover novel modulators of osteoclast differentiation and identified CD300LD, a single-pass transmembrane protein, as a potent driver of osteoclastogenesis. Cd300ld deletion impaired osteoclastogenesis in cell line and primary bone-marrow–derived macrophages. In vivo, myeloid-specific Cd300ld knockout mice exhibited significantly reduced alveolar bone loss and osteoclast numbers in experimental periodontitis, as well as attenuated joint inflammation and bone erosion in arthritis models, whereas bone remodeling during skeletal development remained unaltered. Mechanistically, cholesterol acts as extracellular activator for CD300LD to activate osteoclastogenesis. Cd300ld deficiency intracellularly inhibited phosphorylation of FES, SYK, and STAT3. Consistently, loss of Fes , Syk or Stat3 recapitulated the Cd300ld -deficient phenotypes, establishing a CD300LD–FES–SYK–STAT3 signaling axis essential for osteoclast differentiation. Together, these findings identify CD300LD as a critical, previously unrecognized driver of osteoclastogenesis and highlight it as a promising therapeutic target for inflammatory bone loss.

item.title: Excitonic electrically tunable metaatoms for visible light
item.dc:creator: Janna Wilhelmsen
Longzhu Liu
Harry Miyosi Silalahi
Suraya Kazi
Giancarlo Cincotti
Shangzhi Chen
Dongqing Lin

item.description:
Authors: Janna Wilhelmsen, Longzhu Liu, Harry Miyosi Silalahi, Suraya Kazi, Giancarlo Cincotti, Shangzhi Chen, Dongqing Lin, Yulong Duan, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Phase-gradient metasurfaces shape optical wavefronts through arrays of optical nanoantennas acting as metaatoms. While dynamic tunability forms a major frontier in this area, direct electrical switching of metaatoms operating in the visible has remained challenging. Here, we present an exciton-based metaatom that is electrically tunable and operates in the visible. Its function originates from an excitonic absorption band of a dedoped conjugated polymer, which together with low background permittivity induces optical metallicity in the visible. This allows anisotropic nanostructures to exhibit polarization-dependent optical response through localized surface exciton-polariton resonances, rather than plasmons or dielectric Mie resonances. This function can be fully switched off through reversible doping by small bias potentials, which turns off the exciton-induced metallicity. Our study details the mechanism of these metaatoms and demonstrates their use in electrically tunable phase-gradient metasurfaces for visible light, including erasable and rewritable holograms. This work thereby establishes a class of electrically switchable exciton-based metaatoms and expands the design space of dynamic visible metaoptics.

item.title: Gut microbiota-derived phenylacetylglutamine exacerbates aortic aneurysm and dissection via activating macrophage integrin β1 in male mice
item.dc:creator: Huanhuan Cao
Yanghui Chen
Xiaoyi Liu
Chenwei Lin

item.description:
Authors: Huanhuan Cao, Yanghui Chen, Xiaoyi Liu, Chenwei Lin, Qi Zhang, Jun Yang, Ke Li, Shusi Ding, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Aortic aneurysm and dissection (AAD) are life-threatening cardiovascular diseases with limited therapeutic options. It is essential to identify new risk factors and therapeutic targets for AAD. Recent evidence has highlighted the role of gut microbiota in AAD, yet the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we identify phenylacetylglutamine (PAGln), a gut microbiota–derived metabolite, is associated with increased risk for AAD. Our study illustrates that elevated plasma PAGln levels were independently associated with increased AAD risk in a clinical cohort comprising 1,144 individuals. Exogenous PAGln supplementation exacerbated AAD in male mice, whereas AAV8-mediated hepatic knockdown of Glyat reduced circulating metabolite levels and ameliorated AAD. We further demonstrated that the elevated PAGln levels observed in disease are gut microbiota–dependent in origin. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis revealed that PAGln exacerbates AAD by expanding a pro-inflammatory IL6 (high) macrophage subpopulation. Mechanistically, PAGln directly binds to integrin α5β1 and downregulates the repressive H3K27me3 levels via the integrin α5β1–integrin-linked kinase (ILK)–lysine demethylase 6B (KDM6B) signaling, thereby enhancing IL6 transcriptional permissiveness. Genetic ablation of integrin β1, the receptor for PAGln, effectively ameliorated AAD in male mice. Our findings identify PAGln is associated with increased risk for AAD and reveal its potential as a therapeutic target.

item.dc:creator: Sonia Nicchi

item.description:
Authors: Sonia Nicchi, Suncong Zhou, Mariagrazia Pizza
Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 11960
Abstract: Abstract Klebsiella pneumoniae infections cause hundreds of thousands of deaths annually, yet a licensed vaccine remains elusive. Current strategies targeting capsular polysaccharides and lipopolysaccharides show promise but face limitations due to the complexity of Klebsiella pathogenesis and incomplete understanding of protective immunity. This Review highlights the critical barriers hindering broad protection against K. pneumoniae . We argue that next-generation vaccines require a paradigm shift, integrating antigen discovery, systems immunology and translational models to define conserved protective targets and immune correlates. This holistic strategy is essential to predict vaccine efficacy and finally combat this escalating global health threat.

item.title: Bidirectional control of a metabolic transition by the GID ubiquitin ligase
item.dc:creator: Ka-Yiu Edwin Kong
Cécile Debarnot
Christian Ochs
Matti Myllykoski
Denís Arribas Blanco
Christian Renz
Susmitha Shankar
Vivien A. C. Schoonenberg
item.description:
Authors: Ka-Yiu Edwin Kong, Cécile Debarnot, Christian Ochs, Matti Myllykoski, Denís Arribas Blanco, Christian Renz, Susmitha Shankar, Vivien A. C. Schoonenberg, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 11962
Abstract: Abstract The GID/CTLH ubiquitin ligase is a multisubunit E3 conserved across eukaryotes. GID/CTLH has been implicated in a variety of processes, including metabolic regulation, cell proliferation, embryonic development and cell differentiation. However, our understanding of substrate recognition by GID/CTLH remains incomplete. Here, we characterize the regulation, specificity and functions of the putative substrate receptor Gid11 in budding yeast. We find that upon its expression during the switch of carbon source from glucose to ethanol, Gid11 associates with the core GID complex, likely assembling into a ring-like complex. Through systematic mutagenesis, we identify a negatively charged pocket on Gid11 that binds substrates carrying N-terminal degrons starting with threonine and define the Thr/N-degron motif. Such Thr/N-degrons are exposed upon co-translational removal of the initiator methionine, while escaping N-terminal acetylation. Finally, we show that during the glucose-to-ethanol transition, GID Gid11 targets for degradation factors linked to ribosomal biogenesis, amino acid, nucleotide and central carbon metabolism, opposing the established role of GID during the reverse transition from ethanol to glucose. Authors: Yefan Wang, Peter Nienow, Jaime Otero, Daniel N. Goldberg
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Global glacier recession is driving a rapid increase in the number and volume of ice-marginal lakes, leading to more frequent Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs). The long-term impact of GLOFs on glacier dynamics remains poorly understood, including in Greenland, which holds the largest glacial lake volume in the world. Here, using multi-decadal observations from Isortuarsuup Sermia, Southwest Greenland, we reveal that cyclical GLOFs regulate ice sheet motion. We identify a ‘sawtooth’ pattern of ice-dynamics, whereby multi-year acceleration is terminated abruptly by high-magnitude lake-drainage that resets the glacier to a ‘quiescent’ state for several years. The 2022 event exemplifies this process: the near-terminus ice velocity accelerated briefly from a pre-event baseline of ~200 m a −1 to ~1000 m a −1 before dropping to ~50 m a −1 over subsequent years. Each GLOF releases an immense meltwater volume (mean discharge in 2022 ~17000 m³ s −1 ), carving a ~1.5-km-wide, efficient subglacial channel. This channel enables extensive lowering of the subglacial water pressure, increasing ice–bed friction and suppressing ice motion. As climate warming increases GLOF frequency, this powerful negative feedback will modulate ice sheet motion acting as a brake on ice-dynamics at the margins of the Greenland Ice Sheet.

Abstract: Abstract Regulatory T (Treg) cells contribute to skin homeostasis, but the antigenic targets remain unclear. Whilst CD1a is known to present lipid antigens to effector T cells, the possibility of CD1a presentation to Treg cells us not fully understood. Furthermore, clonally expanded IL-10-producing Treg cells retain their suppressive phenotype in a CD1a-dependent and TCR-dependent manner. Together, these findings show that subsets of Treg cells are directed to self-lipid antigens and CD1a, but show an altered phenotype equipped with pro-inflammatory potential in the setting of psoriasis.

Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 11569
Abstract: Abstract A pause in DNA synthesis that occurs when the replisome encounters an obstacle could lead to genome instability. Although important, systematic identification of replication pause sites is challenging due to their low frequency and delocalised nature. Here we present a single-molecule identification of sites of replisome perturbation across a eukaryotic genome using long-read nanopore sequencing. For each single-molecule replication pause we determine the direction of replication, leading/lagging-strand identity, location and approximate duration, and whether the replisome resumed synthesis. Although pauses are largely diffuse over the genome, they are significantly enriched over transcribed features and correlate with transcription and R-loop levels. Transcription-replication conflicts are more numerous when head-on than co-directional. Finally, we identify genomic loci with a strong bias towards leading over lagging strand pauses, consistent with uncoupling of the helicase from polymerase epsilon. As one such locus overlaps with an epigenetically-regulated gene, we suggest that helicase-polymerase uncoupling resulting from replication pausing could trigger epigenetic switching.

item.description:
Authors: Tiffany Suwatthee, Alex Nazzaro, Rupali Singh, Andrew I. Perault, Somrita Dey, Magdalena Podkowik, Priyanka Mishra, Kathryn Tao, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Staphylococcus aureus is a human bacterial pathogen with an array of molecular mechanisms to evade the action of antibiotics. Within the organism, efflux pumps provide a first-line defense mechanism, enabling broad multidrug resistance across antibiotic classes and the ability for the organism to evolve target-level resistance mechanisms. NorA is a key efflux transporter in S. aureus responsible for conferring resistance to fluoroquinolones, puromycin, and other cytotoxic compounds. Here, we describe an approach to develop peptide efflux pump inhibitors (EPIs) of NorA by leveraging chemical synthesis and design, structure-based insights, and screening approaches to probe NorA pocket engagement and S. aureus growth inhibition. Our cryo-EM structure reveals that a lead peptide NPI-5 inserts deeply into NorA’s substrate binding pocket by using two tryptophan-arginine motifs to bind an anionic patch within NorA, thereby stabilizing the outward-facing conformation of the transporter and halting antibiotic efflux. Further optimization of NPI-5 involving unnatural residues and macrocyclization yielded cNPI-7, a peptide which potentiates fluoroquinolones in vitro and in a murine bacteremia infection model. The successful development of potent and selective peptide-based EPIs provides an approach for inhibiting other efflux systems from pathogenic organisms.

item.title: Autosomal dosage compensation in aneuploidy and cancer involves transcriptional burst regulation
item.dc:creator: Natali Papanicolaou
Sebastian Wettersten
Guilherme Maia
Antonio Lentini
Björn Reinius
item.description:
Authors: Natali Papanicolaou, Sebastian Wettersten, Guilherme Maia, Antonio Lentini, Björn Reinius
Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 12001
Abstract: Abstract Aneuploidy, resulting from whole-chromosome or segmental gains and losses, is generally detrimental to organismal fitness and is strongly associated with tumorigenesis. While sex chromosome aneuploidies are relatively well tolerated due to dedicated allelic dosage compensation mechanisms, the existence of comparable regulatory processes for autosomes remains debated. Here, we investigate transcriptional responses to autosomal aneuploidy and identify widespread dosage compensation across affected chromosomes. Using high-sensitivity allele-resolved single-cell RNA sequencing of monoclonal cell expansions spanning diverse ploidies and degrees of aneuploidy, we uncover consistent transcriptional compensation of both chromosomal gains and losses. This response operates in a region-specific manner across both complete and segmental aneuploidies, revealing an unexpected flexibility in dosage regulation. We show that chromosome losses are compensated through increased transcriptional burst frequency from the remaining allele. Complementary proteomics analyses demonstrate additional buffering at the protein level, resulting in a substantial, though still incomplete, restoration of stoichiometric balance across autosomal aneuploid chromosomes for both copy number gains and losses. Analyses of cancer transcriptomes confirm that compensatory mechanisms are active in human tumours. Together, our findings establish dosage compensation as a genome-wide and dynamic response to gene dose imbalance. This mechanism extends beyond sex chromosomes, supports transcriptional homeostasis, and represents a fundamental and evolutionarily conserved mode of gene regulation active across species and in aneuploid cancer cells.

Authors: Bastien Ducreux, Linda C. Giudice, Marina Sirota, Sally Mortlock, Krina Zondervan, Nilufer Rahmioglu, Merli Saare, Serdar E. Bulun, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Endometriosis is a chronic inflammatory disease affecting 10% of women, characterized by the growth of endometrial-like tissue outside the uterus. Through a genome-wide DNA methylation meta-analysis of nine independent cohorts ( n = 1138 samples), we show an epigenetic dichotomy: the eutopic endometrium of endometriosis cases shows no significant divergence from healthy controls, whereas ectopic lesions exhibit massive, consistent hyper/hypomethylation. We identify 1824 differentially methylated regions targeting the HOX clusters, ESR1 , and GATA2 , key regulators of cell differentiation and hormonal response. This suggests that endometriotic cells possess an epigenetic identity distinct from normal endometrial cells. While most alterations reflect biological mechanisms shared across anatomical sites, distinct signatures exist between lesion types. By harmonizing independent datasets, our study provides a high-resolution molecular map of lesions and strengthens the evidence that DNA methylation drives endometriosis biology.

Authors: Mengyang Zhou, Mary-Louise Timmermans, Elizabeth Yankovsky, Michael D. Tyka, Matthew C. Long
Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 11411
Abstract: Abstract Ocean-based geochemical CO 2 removal approaches, including ocean alkalinity enhancement (OAE) and direct ocean removal (DOR), have received attention for their potential to remove billion-ton-scale amounts of CO 2 from the atmosphere. Their viability at scale depends on efficiency. Here, we develop a unified framework for evaluating the efficiencies of ocean geochemical perturbations: OAE adds alkalinity, DOR removes dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC), and combined alkalinity and DIC addition (ADA) adds both simultaneously. Using a global ocean biogeochemical model, we map global and seasonal DOR efficiency and compare it with OAE efficiency. Further, we show that OAE and DOR simulations can be combined to quantify the effect of simultaneous perturbations in alkalinity and DIC. This enables direct quantification of the oceanic fate of ADA perturbations from approaches such as enhanced rock weathering, riverine alkalinity enhancement and accelerated weathering of limestone. In these approaches, the added alkalinity partially equilibrates with CO 2 before entering the ocean, effectively adding both alkalinity and DIC.

Abstract: Abstract In contrast to well-established C–C migration rearrangements of spiro[indole-3,3’-pyrrolidine] systems, analogous transformations involving isomeric spiro[indole-3,2’-pyrrolidine] frameworks remain unexplored. Abstract: Abstract Neuroblastoma (NB) arises from neural crest-derived cells of the sympathoadrenal lineage, yet how predisposing genetic lesions influence early human development remains poorly understood. Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Detecting active phage–bacteria interactions in natural microbial communities remains a major limitation for understanding their ecological dynamics and associated co-evolutionary processes. Here, we apply metaHi-C, a chromosome conformation capture method, to resolve active virus–host associations in a freshwater microbial community. From >900 microbial and >33,000 viral Hi-C–assembled genomes, we identify 100 high-confidence phage–host linkages spanning major freshwater bacterial lineages, including Limnohabitans , Acidimicrobium , Synechococcus , Candidatus Nanopelagicus, Candidatus Planktophila, Candidatus Methylopumilus, and Polynucleobacter . The inferred networks reveal signatures consistent with diverse infection patterns, including broad-host-range phages, cellular-level co-infection, kill-the-winner-like dynamics, and one-to-one interactions. These ecological patterns are associated with signatures of diversifying selection in host-interaction genes, consistent with host-range expansion, alongside conserved genomic regions in broad-host-range and co-infecting phages, indicating functional constraints on essential infection modules. Together, these results demonstrate that metaHi-C enables the direct detection of active phage–host associations within a community snapshot, and that, when combined with longitudinal metagenomic recruitment analyses, this approach can link community-level infection dynamics to underlying evolutionary processes, revealing how these forces shape population dynamics of freshwater bacteria.

Abstract: Abstract Modern dietary patterns, particularly those low in fermentable fiber, are associated with intestinal dysbiosis and increased susceptibility to allergic disease, yet individuals exposed to similar diets often display markedly different outcomes. This variability suggests that protective commensal microbes may persist in some hosts, but the mechanisms that maintain these bacteria and enable their immunoregulatory effects remain unclear. Here, we show that Bifidobacterium induces self-recognizing, T cell–dependent immunoglobulin A (IgA) that enhances its mucosal adhesion and persistence under fiber-deprived conditions. Together, these findings reveal a self-reinforcing host–microbial mutualism in which adaptive IgA preserves, rather than eliminates, beneficial commensals to maintain immune homeostasis.

Abstract: Abstract Chemical substitution is an effective strategy to enhance the desired performances of materials based on known structural prototypes. However, it almost invariably introduces intrinsic defects, such as vacancies and twinning defects, which couple with dopants and obscure or degrade the intrinsic properties. Therefore, chemical substitution that enables atomically precise engineering of materials without generating defect structures remains challenging. Here, we propose a quasi-degenerate cation occupation strategy to overcome this detrimental coupling and successfully apply it to the langasite-family nonlinear optical (NLO) crystal, La 3 TiGa 5 O 14 (LGTi). Therein, the cross-site occupation of Ti and Ti 3+ /Ti 4+ redox flexibility improves the kinetic accessibility of oxygen-vacancy ( V O ) defects associated with cation disorder, enabling their removal during oxidative annealing. Abstract: Abstract We experience our limbs as our own, but how does the brain generate this fundamental sense of body ownership? Previous studies have relied mainly on fMRI or lesion mapping, providing a static view of the neural mechanisms underlying body ownership. Abstract: Abstract Against the backdrop of global efforts to address climate change and promote carbon neutrality, parks, as Nature-based solutions, are often underestimated in their collective carbon sequestration function. Abstract: Abstract Ageing is characterised by widespread cellular and molecular dysregulation including broad changes to gene expression. Abstract: Abstract Color center spins in diamond nanostructures are a key resource for emerging quantum technologies. Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 11925
Abstract: Abstract Multi-ome mapping technologies for precise comprehensive characterization of tissues at high spatial resolutions are crucial for providing insights into tissue heterogeneity and microenvironment within spatial context. However, proteome mapping technologies lag far behind other transcriptome (genome) mapping technologies. Here we report an Ultralow-volume, Shallow, Microwell plate-based voxel Collection and Processing coupled with mass spectrometry (MS) method, termed USMCP-MS, for robust scalable proteome mapping of tissues at high spatial resolutions. This method was built upon the design of an ultralow-volume, shallow 96-well plate for robust rapid collection and processing of single voxels. Abstract: Abstract Midbrain dopaminergic neurons (mDA) are selectively lost in Parkinson’s disease, driving sustained efforts to generate bona fide mDA neurons from human-induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) for replacement therapy. While morphogen gradients and transcription factors have been extensively studied, extracellular regulators remain largely overlooked. Here, we identify the heparan sulfate-modifying enzymes SULF1 and SULF2 as essential for establishing mDA neuron identity in vitro. Mechanistically, we partially explain the changed patterning to aberrant FGF signaling and demonstrate that FGF inhibition redirects cells toward midbrain fates, however without restoring ventral identity. These findings establish a critical role for SULF1/2 in mDA neuron in vitro differentiation and uncover a previously unrecognized layer of extracellular control over neural patterning.

Abstract: Abstract Stature is a key indicator of pediatric health, yet the molecular and metabolic architecture governing childhood growth remains incompletely defined. We conduct genome-wide association analyses of stature from birth to childhood (574,580 measurements; 72,704 Norwegian children) and integrate UK Biobank data (age 10 and adulthood). We uncover life-stage shifts in the genetics of stature, identifying previously not identified childhood-specific effects including variants near GLP1R with BMI-independent effects, and reveal three temporal clusters - Infancy and Childhood clusters enriched for endocrine and metabolic pathways, and a Lifetime growth cluster enriched for skeletal biology. Proteome analysis reveals that prepubertal height is associated with widespread changes in the circulation, identifying 106 height-associated proteins and linking IGF1, IGF2, and IGFBP3 levels to childhood-height polygenic scores. Mendelian randomization shows that reduced fetal growth and taller prepubertal height increase type 2 diabetes risk, independent of adult stature. These findings uncover developmental stage-specific genetic and proteomic influences on child-growth and links to adult metabolic health.

Authors: Jianhong Lin, Nicolas Delpierre, Cyrille Rathgeber, Hai Ren, Jian-Guo Huang, Frank Berninger, Xiaobo Li, Qianqian Ma
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Late spring frost is an intensifying climatic disturbance, yet how frost damage to different organs (leaves and flowers) reshapes reproductive phenology and generates carry-over effects remains unclear. Using 259,732 phenological observations across eight European woody species spanning 1950–2024, we show that foliar frost damage shortened the fruit development period (FDP; the interval from flowering to fruit maturity) by 1.6 days, driven by delayed flowering and advanced fruit maturity. Conversely, floral frost damage prolonged FDP by 1.3 days through delayed fruit maturity, with both effects strengthening under greater frost severity. Accounting for anomalously warm conditions in the frost year substantially reduced the estimated delays in flowering and subsequent-year phenology, indicating that neglecting climatic context leads to overestimation of frost effects. These findings reveal organ-specific pathways through which frost damage reshapes reproductive phenology while generating limited carry-over effects, refining current understanding of phenological responses under climate change.

Abstract: Abstract How do our brains manage to store our everyday experiences into memory? Neurons in the human temporal lobe that respond to the concept of an individual person or object have been shown to provide the semantic building blocks for episodic memory. Unlike rodent place cells, which can acquire preferred firing locations during exploration of new environments according to their pre-existing preferred sequence of activation, human concept neurons are tuned to specific semantic contents before learning starts. Consequently, pre-existing firing sequences correlate with consecutive place fields in rodents, but not with sequences of events in human experience. Thus, in contrast to reactivation of rodent place cells, reactivation of human concept cells does not reflect sequences of events in human experience.

Abstract: Abstract Benzoxaboroles (BoBs) such as acoziborole feature a boron-heterocyclic core and are an important innovation in the development of drugs against a range of pathogens and other pathologies. Abstract: Abstract In contrast to the well-explored peripheral functionalization of benzene, its skeletal alteration remains underdeveloped. Here, we report a highly distorted benzenium cation, 2,3-dihydroxy-1,4,6-triamino-5-nitrobenzenium (TANBC + ), featuring a ring twist angle of 35.91° and a ring C-C bond length of 1.540 Å, both rank the highest among all benzenium cations. Consequently, instead of undergoing peripheral functionalization like typical benzenium cations, TANBC + participates in three distinct benzene ring reconstruction pathways or remains inert under standard electrophilic substitution conditions. Moreover, despite its distorted structure, TANBC + exhibits excellent ambient stability, stabilized by extensive hydrogen bonding, and can be synthesized readily without harsh conditions usually required for conventional benzenium cations. This work not only introduces a new strategy for benzene reconstruction but also redefines the role of benzenium cations from mediators of peripheral functionalization to promoters of skeletal alteration, thereby advancing the fundamental chemistry of benzene.

Abstract: Abstract Land-use and land-cover change (LULCC) is altering greenhouse gas (GHG) dynamics in coastal wetlands, yet how these responses vary among ecosystems and conversion pathways remains uncertain. Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 11879
Abstract: Abstract Coherent extreme-ultraviolet (XUV) light is a central tool in modern photon science, probing the electronic, chemical and structural properties of matter. High-harmonic generation can extend the reach of laser sources into this spectral range, but the achievable photon flux falls sharply as photon energy increases. We show experimentally and theoretically that plasma-core-induced self-guiding of a visible-wavelength driver in helium sustains high intensity and favorable phase matching over an extended propagation length. We achieve a conversion efficiency of up to 10 −6 in a single high-harmonic line and phase-matched emission extending to 100 eV. With less than 10 W of average power at 516 nm from a frequency-doubled ytterbium laser, we generate 1.8 × 10 11 photons s −1 within 2 % bandwidth at 13.5 nm (91.8 eV), exceeding previous reports by more than an order of magnitude. These results establish a power-scalable XUV platform for actinic metrology, spectroscopy and coherent imaging.

item.title: Accelerating high-throughput catalyst screening by direct generation of equilibrium adsorption structures
item.dc:creator: Songze Huo
Xiao-Ming Cao
item.description:
Authors: Songze Huo, Xiao-Ming Cao
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract The adsorption energy serves as a crucial descriptor for the large-scale screening of catalysts. Nevertheless, the limited distribution of training data for the extensively utilised machine learning interatomic potential, predominantly sourced from near-equilibrium structures, results in unreliable adsorption structures and consequent adsorption energy predictions. In this context, we present DBCata, a deep generative model that integrates a periodic Brownian-bridge framework with an equivariant graph neural network to establish a low-dimensional transition manifold between unrelaxed and DFT-relaxed structures, without requiring explicit energy or force information. Upon training, DBCata effectively generates high-fidelity adsorption geometries, achieving an interatomic distance mean absolute error of 0.035 Å on the dataset from Catalysis-Hub, which is approximately 70% lower than that of the current state-of-the-art machine learning potential models. Moreover, the corresponding DFT accuracy can be improved within 0.1 eV in 94% of instances by identifying and refining anomalous predictions through a hybrid chemical-heuristic and self-supervised outlier detection approach. We demonstrate that DBCata enables accelerated high-throughput computational screening for alloy catalysts in the oxygen reduction reaction, highlighting the potential of DBCata as a powerful tool for catalyst design and optimisation.

item.description:
Authors: Yueyun Chen, Xin Yi Ling, Jared J. Lodico, Tristan P. O’Neill, B. C. Regan, Matthew Mecklenburg
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract As electronic devices are engineered at increasingly smaller length scales, new nanoscopic metrologies are needed. Measuring nanoscale temperatures and pressures is challenging as physical contact inevitably perturbs the system, and collecting far-field thermal radiation limits the spatial resolution. Kikuchi diffraction thermometry (KDTh), a non-contact scanning electron microscope (SEM) technique, can sensitively map nanoscale temperatures. Local lattice changes measured by Kikuchi pattern fitting enable translating volumetric strain to temperature via the material’s coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE). Measurements on Joule-heated graphite come from rastering a 5.5-nm electron probe across the sample, achieving a ~ 0.01% fractional precision and 2.2 K/ $$\sqrt{{{\rm{Hz}}}}$$ Hz temperature sensitivity. KDTh offers superior sensitivity by fitting the entire Kikuchi pattern, instead of a particular Kikuchi band or interband angle. Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) techniques can achieve a similar precision, but electron-transparency limits their applications. KDTh can operate in both transmission and reflection modes to cost-effectively accommodate a variety of samples.

item.description:
Authors: Moonyoung Kang, Mohamed Omar Kamileen, Yoko Nakamura, John P. Hamilton, Gyumin Kang, Bruno Huettel, Jens Wurlitzer, Sarah Heinicke, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 11878
Abstract: Abstract Tabernanthe iboga (iboga) is the source of voacangine, which is widely used as a semi-synthetic starting material for the anti-addiction agent ibogaine. Despite extensive investigation of voacangine biosynthesis, production of this compound cannot be reconstituted in a heterologous host, suggesting that one or more enzymes required for biosynthesis are missing. Additionally, T. iboga produces ibophyllidine, a pyrroloindole alkaloid that utilizes the same upstream precursor as voacangine, but is a member of a structurally distinct alkaloid class. Here we use bulk and single cell gene expression from leaf and root tissue to identify the unknown enzymes from these two pathways. We identify two additional enzymes that enable biosynthesis of voacangine in a heterologous host. The missing enzymes includes a pathogenesis-related (PR)10 family protein that likely catalyzes cyclization of a transient intermediate. Careful analysis of gene expression profiles in leaf and root also enabled the discovery of four additional enzymes that convert an upstream intermediate to ibophyllidine. This work reveals the chemical logic that generates two distinct alkaloid scaffolds in this important medicinal plant.
